clue.text: Work at taking in a drama

indicators.note: one piece taking in another means it holds the other inside it

parts.note: to ply a trade is to work at it
taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor or student is busy rehearsing a stage drama.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama staged in a theatre is a stage work, a synonym.

clue.text: Predict he's taking on Yard after getting support

indicators.note: the following pieces come after the support in the answer
taking on means adding the next piece at the end

parts.note: a prop is a support
the word taken as written, without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: A detective predicts he will join Scotland Yard once he has backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yard' suggests Scotland Yard, the London police; here it is only the unit.
explanation.definitionFit: To foretell the future is to make a forecast, a synonym.

clue.text: Rise in support given to a new nurse?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading the support word upwards, backwards

parts.note: a leg is a support, as of a table

explanation.surface: A newly qualified nurse gets a pay rise and some backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rise in' turns LEG into GEL. The question mark admits nurses are only fondly called this.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind, caring person, especially a nurse, is often affectionately called a heavenly being.

clue.text: Quick way to switch off after electrical problem

indicators.note: the switching-off piece comes after the electrical fault in the answer

parts.note: a short is a short circuit, an electrical fault
to cut the power is to switch it off

explanation.surface: After a fault in the wiring, someone advises a fast way to kill the power.
explanation.definitionFit: A quicker route than the usual one, or any time-saving method, is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Drunk to secure romance in dance in Inverness

parts.note: high means intoxicated
to land a deal is to secure it
a fling is a brief romance

explanation.surface: A tipsy person hopes to win a brief romance at a dance in the Scottish city.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively solo Scottish country dance is performed at Highland games; Inverness is a Highland city.

clue.text: Bird starts to rummage on waste container

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters

parts.note: a bin holds rubbish

explanation.surface: A bird begins foraging on top of a rubbish bin.
explanation.definitionFit: The red-breasted songbird is one kind of bird.

clue.text: Whip about to meet pair of Liberals getting derisive comment

parts.note: the cat is the cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip
ca, circa, means about
L is Liberal, so two of them are LL

explanation.surface: A party whip, about to meet two Liberal MPs, gets heckled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip' suggests the parliamentary whip in the surface; it is the lash.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrill whistle or jeer of disapproval from a crowd is a mocking remark.

clue.text: Watch maybe not showing minutes produces row

indicators.note: letters not showing are left out of the word

parts.note: a watch is one example of a timer

explanation.surface: A watch with no minutes displayed causes an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' reads as a quarrel in the surface; it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A level or rank of seating, as in a stadium, is a line of seats.

clue.text: The best prison, we hear, will offer outdoor excursion

indicators.note: we hear means the words are said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: the pick of a bunch is the best of it; nick is British slang for a prison or police station

explanation.surface: The finest jail will offer prisoners a day out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nick' is British slang for a prison or police station.
explanation.definitionFit: A meal eaten outside on an outing is a trip with food, the noun's usual sense.

clue.text: One probing two songs missing intros — still an issue?

indicators.note: one piece probing another pushes into its middle
each copy of the song word loses its opening letter
two asks for the song word written out twice

parts.note: a song is a song, taken one at a time and doubled
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A singer probing a pair of half-heard songs wonders whether a dispute remains unresolved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two' gives SONGSONG; 'missing intros' drops each first S to leave ONGONG; 'probing' sends I into the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something still in progress or not yet settled continues, which is the adjective's meaning.

clue.text: Sailor returned before the swim

indicators.note: the turned sailor stands before the next word
returned means the sailor's abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A seaman comes back to shore before going for a dip.
explanation.definitionFit: To go for a dip in the sea or a pool can be described as a swim, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Girl seen between Rachel and Ena?

indicators.note: the name is seen in the stretch between the start of the first name and the end of the second, skipping the joining word

explanation.surface: A third woman appears among two friends with old-fashioned names, perhaps from a soap.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'Rachel' into the start of 'Ena', jumping the 'and'; the question mark admits the liberty. Ena Sharples was a character in the British soap Coronation Street.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name is clued by the generic word for a female, as crosswords often do.

clue.text: Article on board ship following a straight course

indicators.note: a passenger on board a vessel is inside it

parts.note: a liner is a large passenger ship
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece aboard a vessel describes it sailing dead ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving in a line, without curving, is the adjective's geometric sense.

clue.text: Panic diverted this year

indicators.note: letters diverted are sent off their usual route, rearranged

explanation.surface: A panic has been averted, or redirected, this year.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild, uncontrolled emotion or frenzy is a synonym for alarm.

clue.text: Awful villainy close in hi-tech area

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Terrible wrongdoing is happening nearby in a district of technology firms.
explanation.definitionFit: The Californian region around San Jose is famous as the home of computer and internet companies.

clue.text: Felt ale, newly brewed, should get promotional material

indicators.note: letters newly brewed are mixed up afresh

explanation.surface: A brewery promoting its fresh ale hands out a flyer.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed handout or flyer advertising something is advertising material.

clue.text: Thinking cannily when Egyptian King's heading for Egypt

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as he left
Tut, Tutankhamun, was an Egyptian pharaoh

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A shrewd pharaoh plans his journey towards Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd and quick-witted describes someone who reasons in a canny way.

clue.text: Argument about a bar's latest set of charges

indicators.note: the quarrel word goes about, around, the other letters

parts.note: a tiff is a petty quarrel
taken as written

indicators.note: the latest letter of a word is its last one

explanation.surface: A row breaks out over a pub's newest price list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps TIFF around A and R, the end of 'bar's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A published list of prices or duties is a schedule of fees, the noun's ordinary meaning.

clue.text: Elected, with upturn in support, in Asian country

parts.note: a candidate who is elected is in

indicators.note: in a down clue an upturn reads the support word upwards, backwards

parts.note: aid is support

explanation.surface: A government is elected and support rises in an Asian nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The south Asian republic is one nation of that continent.

clue.text: Crime seen in financial newspaper?

parts.note: the pink business daily is the Financial Times, so its title with the article and initials, run together, spells an offence

explanation.surface: A story of wrongdoing is reported in the business press.
explanation.walkthrough: The Financial Times is known as THE FT; run together it spells the answer, a crime, with the question mark flagging the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is a criminal offence, and the paper's short title happens to spell it.

clue.text: Little hesitation about the time — very keen

indicators.note: the hesitation goes about, around, the time word

parts.note: er is a brief hesitant sound in speech
an age is a time or period

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates only briefly about the timing, being so enthusiastic.
explanation.definitionFit: Enthusiastic and impatient to do something is the adjective's sense.

clue.text: Round? Very — almost entirely egg-shaped

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: all means entirely, as in all alone

explanation.surface: Asked whether something is round, someone says it is very nearly egg-shaped.
explanation.definitionFit: An elliptical outline, like that of an egg, is the adjective's literal sense.

clue.text: Acceptable video about a learner

indicators.note: the video word goes about, around, the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A film about someone learning is deemed suitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps VID around A and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Something legitimate or sound is admissible, the adjective's sense.

clue.text: Number, say, encountered in Bury

indicators.note: something encountered in a word is found inside it

parts.note: to inter is to bury
say means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: A figure, perhaps, came across in the Lancashire town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' looks like the Lancashire town; it is the verb, and 'encountered in' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole number with no fractional part is a kind of number.

clue.text: Disinclination to shift hospital: greatly upset about that

indicators.note: the jumbled word goes about, around, the piece just named
upset means the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A patient refuses to move hospital and is very distressed about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns GREATLY into LETARGY, and 'about that' puts it around H.
explanation.definitionFit: Sluggishness, a lack of energy to get moving, is the noun's meaning.

clue.text: Live action's beginning in region

parts.note: to live is to be, and are is a form of be

indicators.note: a word's beginning is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Live action is starting up in a district.
explanation.definitionFit: A district or zone is a synonym for a stretch of territory.
